title: CommonJS
body:
The specification behind the [[CommonJS Module]] system — the `require()` / `module.exports` convention that [[Node.js]] adopted for server-side JavaScript before the language had modules of its own.

It was designed for a server environment, where files are read synchronously off local disk, so `require()` blocks until the module is loaded. That assumption is fine on a server and unworkable in a browser, which is part of why browser code needed bundling in the first place, and why the language eventually standardised on ES modules (`import`/`export`) instead.

Both systems now coexist in Node, distinguished by file extension (`.cjs` vs `.mjs`) or by the `type` field in `package.json`. See [[Module]].
